audience.text: Python developers building 3D content pipelines, especially for 3D printing, CAD visualization, and lightweight 3D asset processing.

capabilities.text: Imports OBJ, STL, glTF/GLB, COLLADA, and 3MF files using Scene.open() with automatic format detection from file extension or explicit FileFormat.
capabilities.title: Load multiple 3D formats

capabilities.text: Exports scenes to OBJ, STL, glTF/GLB, and 3MF using Scene.save() with format-specific options for compression, coordinate system, and unit scaling.
capabilities.title: Export to common 3D formats

capabilities.text: Construct hierarchical scene graphs using Scene, Node, and Entity objects with independent transforms per node.
capabilities.title: Build and traverse scene graphs

capabilities.text: Create meshes from control points and polygons, convert primitives to meshes, and modify geometry via Mesh.control_points and Mesh.create_polygon().
capabilities.title: Create and edit mesh geometry

capabilities.text: Assign LambertMaterial, PhongMaterial, or PbrMaterial to nodes and set diffuse, specular, albedo, metallic, and roughness properties.
capabilities.title: Assign and configure materials

capabilities.text: Build keyframe animations using AnimationClip, AnimationNode, and KeyframeSequence, and store skeletal bind-pose data with Pose and related types.
capabilities.title: Support keyframe animation

limitations.text: FBX import is experimental and FBX export is not implemented; FbxExporter.save() raises NotImplementedError.
COLLADA export is not reachable through Scene.save() due to exporter lookup order issues.
Scene.render() and the entire aspose.threed.render module raise NotImplementedError; this library does not render scenes to images.
Texture and TextureBase raise NotImplementedError on construction; image-backed textures cannot be created.
Mesh boolean operations (union, difference, intersect) raise NotImplementedError.
NURBS curve evaluation and surface-to-mesh conversion raise NotImplementedError.

problems_solved.text: Enables programmatic creation, modification, and export of 3D scenes using a pure-Python API without requiring external SDKs or native binaries.
Supports common 3D file formats used in 3D printing and web workflows (OBJ, STL, glTF/GLB, COLLADA, 3MF) through a unified Scene/Node/Mesh object model.
Provides parameterized primitives (Box, Sphere, Cylinder, etc.) and direct mesh editing capabilities for rapid prototyping and geometry generation.

product_summary.text: Aspose.3D FOSS for Python is a pure-Python, MIT-licensed library for loading, constructing, and exporting 3D scenes without native dependencies.

uncertainties: The exact set of formats supported beyond those explicitly listed in format facts is unclear; some option classes exist but are not dispatchable.
Whether the library supports importing FBX files in practice beyond tokenizer tests is uncertain.
The behavior of Scene.save() when no format can be inferred from filename or explicit FileFormat is not documented in facts.

workflows.name: Import and inspect 3D scenes
workflows.text: Load OBJ, STL, glTF, COLLADA, or 3MF files using Scene.open() and inspect geometry, nodes, and materials.

workflows.name: Export scenes to 3D formats
workflows.text: Save scenes to OBJ, STL, glTF/GLB, or 3MF using Scene.save() with format-specific SaveOptions for fine-grained control.

workflows.name: Build scenes from primitives
workflows.text: Create parameterized primitives like Box, Sphere, or Cylinder, convert them to meshes via to_mesh(), and attach materials.

workflows.name: Construct meshes from control points
workflows.text: Build custom meshes by adding control points and polygons, then attach materials and save to target formats.

workflows.name: Assign materials to 3D entities
workflows.text: Attach LambertMaterial, PhongMaterial, or PbrMaterial to nodes and configure diffuse, specular, albedo, metallic, and roughness properties.

workflows.name: Triangulate polygon meshes
workflows.text: Triangulate arbitrary polygon data using PolygonModifier.triangulate() for compatibility with formats requiring triangle geometry.
